 Brazoria County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0030
 Ashley Duncan, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Plaintiff's Original Petition
Filed:
June 25, 2024
Plaintiff's counsel:
Candice Smith, Dunn & Acosta LLP
PARTIES
Plaintiff Ashley Duncan is an individual residing in Texas who was the driver and insured party involved in the motor vehicle
collision described below. Defendant is the automobile liability insurer that issued the policy under which Plaintiff seeks
coverage and benefits, and which is subject to suit in Texas.
FACTS
On July 24, 2023, Plaintiff was lawfully operating a vehicle on a public roadway in Katy. Another vehicle, operated by an
adverse driver whose conduct is at issue in this matter, moved into the lane occupied by Plaintiff while changing lanes without
adequate signaling or clearance. The vehicles made contact in a sideswipe collision that forced Plaintiff's car off its path. Plaintiff
reported the collision promptly and submitted the claim to Defendant under the applicable coverage. Defendant has not paid the
benefits owed under the policy in a timely and reasonable manner.
NEGLIGENCE
The adverse driver owed a duty to exercise ordinary care when changing lanes, including checking blind spots, signaling, and
yielding to vehicles already in the lane. That duty was breached. Defendant, as the insurer, owed Plaintiff a duty of good faith and
fair dealing in investigating, evaluating, and paying covered claims, and Defendant breached that duty by failing to conduct a
reasonable investigation and by delaying or underpaying the claim without a reasonable basis.
DAMAGES
As a direct result of the collision, Plaintiff suffered a concussion with headaches, dizziness, and cognitive difficulty, requiring
medical treatment and time away from work. Plaintiff has incurred medical expenses, lost earnings, and pain and suffering.
Plaintiff seeks recovery of policy benefits, statutory damages available under Texas law for unfair claim settlement practices, and
attorney's fees. Plaintiff demands judgment in the amount of $120,000.00, together with pre-judgment and post-judgment interest
and costs of court.
